findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the CI Bedrock arm obtains AWS credentials on a GitHub-hosted runner (name the mechanism, e.g. OIDC role assumption via aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials to a dedicated role, or static keys in a secret) — the S7 EC2 instance-role precedent is not reachable from `ubuntu-latest` — AND state how the region resolves (REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION plus AWS_DEFAULT_REGION per bug rebar:a574), since the [llm.model_classes]-only config file supplies neither.
evidence: Plan: 'S7 … already established scoped Bedrock access for the review-bot container — reuse that precedent rather than inventing a second access path.'

rebar:9249 evidence: caller identity from INSIDE compose-review-bot-1 is `assumed-role/rebar-gerrit-instance-role/<instance-id>` via IMDS — an instance-role path specific to the EC2 host, not available to a GitHub-hosted runner.
external-integration.yml:32 `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` — GitHub-hosted runner, no instance role, no IMDS to the review-bot host.

rebar:a574 (closed): 'IMDS is NOT the region source … region must be configured explicitly no matter what IMDS does'; setting only REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION was insufficient — AWS_DEFAULT_REGION also required, else NoRegionError.
Plan states the config file sets ONLY `[llm.model_classes]`; region (REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION / AWS_DEFAULT_REGION) is not part of that table.
Evidence class: Contradicted (instance-role reuse for a GitHub runner) + Unverified (no named CI credential mechanism).
findings.finding: The Bedrock arm's CI credential path and region resolution are asserted but not established for a GitHub-hosted runner. The plan says to 'reuse the S7 access precedent,' but S7 (rebar:9249) grants an EC2 INSTANCE ROLE reachable via IMDS from the review-bot container — a path a `ubuntu-latest` GitHub-hosted runner (external-integration.yml:32) cannot use. The plan names no mechanism (OIDC role assumption vs. static keys in a secret) by which the runner enters the AWS credential chain. Separately, bug rebar:a574 (closed) established that IMDS does NOT supply an AWS region and that Bedrock hard-fails with NoRegionError unless a region is set explicitly; the plan's config file sets only `[llm.model_classes]` and names no region for the CI Bedrock arm.
findings.location: Approach paragraph 4 ('Bedrock authenticates from the AWS credential chain … reuse that precedent'); AC line 'The Bedrock arm authenticates via the AWS credential chain (not an API key), reusing the S7 access precedent'
scenarios: The Bedrock matrix arm is authored per the plan; on a GitHub-hosted runner it has no way to assume rebar-gerrit-instance-role, so the credential presence check finds nothing and the arm skips (or errors) — the very Bedrock coverage the epic wants never runs.
AWS credentials are wired but no region is set; BedrockProvider construction raises NoRegionError before any model call, and the arm fails for a reason unrelated to the provider seam under test.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, replace 'reuse the S7 precedent' for the CI runner with a concrete GitHub-runner credential path — e.g. configure OIDC (`permissions: id-token: write` + aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials) to assume a scoped Bedrock role modeled on S7's policy — and set both AWS_DEFAULT_REGION and REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION as job env for the Bedrock arm. Add an AC that the Bedrock arm resolves a region and fails loudly (typed LLMConfigError, per rebar:a574) rather than skipping silently when the region is absent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile S10's CI-workflow scope with epic 061c's declared contract: either note in S10 that it extends the epic's live-coverage goal onto the external-integration/prompt-eval workflows (a surface the epic Scope did not enumerate and its manifest marked 'dep absent .github/workflows/'), or confirm with the epic that CI-matrix coverage is intended epic scope alongside the S8 review-bot dogfood and S6 parity.
evidence: Epic 061c Scope lists src/rebar/llm/* files, infra/terraform/*, docs, pyproject.toml — it does NOT list .github/workflows/external-integration.yml or prompt-eval.yml.
Epic 061c plan-review manifest entry: 'dep absent .github/workflows/' — the epic's contract treated CI workflows as outside its dependency set.

Epic 061c live-coverage ACs are carried by the review-bot dogfood (AC 'the review bot's most recent LLM-Review vote ... carries Bedrock provenance', 'production review bot votes LLM-Review using Bedrock') and by S6 parity — not by a per-provider external-test matrix.

S10 goal ('provider as a MATRIX DIMENSION of the external suite') is a reasonable instantiation of the epic goal 'first-class Anthropic AND Bedrock, best-effort OpenAI-compatible' and uses the epic-established REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE mechanism — so this is consistent extension, contradicting no parent AC.
findings.finding: S10 centers its deliverable on CI workflow files (.github/workflows/external-integration.yml and prompt-eval.yml) that the parent epic 061c never enumerates in its Scope, and which the epic's plan-review manifest explicitly recorded as 'dep absent .github/workflows/'. The epic's own live-multi-provider-coverage obligation is discharged by siblings S8 (review-bot Bedrock cutover) and S6 (parity harness), not by a CI matrix. This is an enumeration/scope-boundary mismatch, not a contradiction of any epic AC — the epic goal ('live-grounded confidence across every provider we hold credentials for') plausibly admits it — so it is coached, not blocking.
findings.location: S10 Approach / Acceptance Criteria (vs epic 061c 'Scope' and its plan-review manifest 'dep absent .github/workflows/')
scenarios: Epic close-time review checks S10's delivered files against the epic's enumerated Scope and finds CI-workflow work the epic never listed, raising a spurious scope-growth flag.
A reviewer treats S10 as out-of-epic because the epic's dogfooding mechanism was named as the review bot, not the external CI suite.

findings.finding: The Approach bullet 'Decide and record whether every provider runs on every trigger, or whether non-default providers run on a reduced cadence or a reduced case subset' defers a real design choice to the executor without stating a default, so the plan itself does not settle the cadence.
